subskill: Store and retrieve app configuration information by using Azure App Configuration
question: A Python provider’s last secret retrieval and ordinary refresh check both complete at t=0. It uses a versionless Key Vault reference, refresh_interval=60 and secret_refresh_interval=300. The app calls refresh() only at t=120,240,360,..., and each call succeeds within one second. The sentinel stays unchanged; a new enabled secret version is stored at t=200. Which is the first listed call whose timing permits the secret to be re-resolved?

answerChoices.text: Only a call after the sentinel changes

explanation: The t=360 call is the first listed call after the 300-second secret interval, and the ordinary 60-second interval has also elapsed.
deepExplanation: The calls are 120 seconds apart and complete within one second, so each later call is more than 60 seconds after the previous ordinary check. At t=120 and t=240 the 300-second secret interval has not elapsed. At t=360 both interval conditions are satisfied. The secret refresh mechanism does not require a sentinel change. This schedule avoids the unresolved SDK ordering question that arises when the secret interval is due but the ordinary interval is not; it does not assert which check the implementation performs first.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.A: t=240 is an ordinary-refresh-eligible call, but only 240 seconds have passed since the secret was retrieved. A shorter secret_refresh_interval could permit that call; the specified value is 300 seconds.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.C: A changed sentinel is the publication trigger for watched ordinary settings. The documented independent secret refresh exists for rotated secrets whose App Configuration reference and sentinel remain unchanged, so that ordinary-setting condition is not required here.
